moduleTitle: Using the REST API in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Generate and use a Testim REST API key to authenticate requests.
Distinguish REST API authentication from additional user authorization for encrypted credentials.

elements.description: API access is a professional feature, available only to projects on the professional plan — it isn't something every project tier has access to by default.
Go to Settings → API, click Generate API Key, and name it. The key's value is shown once; you must copy it immediately and click Done, since that display is the only time the raw value is visible.

Use Authorization: Bearer followed by the copied API key, which already has its PAK- prefix. For encrypted-credential runs/results, additionally provide an authorized user’s access key in X-User-Access-Key. This does not replace normal API authentication or grant permissions to an unauthorized user.

bulletPoints: API key value is shown exactly once at generation time — copy it immediately.
Bearer authenticates the API request; X-User-Access-Key additionally identifies a user permitted to use encrypted credentials.

examPitfalls.title: Navigating away before copying a newly generated API key
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Generating an API key, clicking Done without copying the value, then having no way to retrieve it afterward.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The API key value is displayed only once, at generation time. Copy it immediately — if lost, a new key must be generated instead of recovering the old one.

examPitfalls.title: Treating user access as replacement API authentication
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Omitting the standard Bearer authentication or assuming an access key bypasses encrypted-credential permissions.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Authenticate with the API key and additionally supply the permitted user’s X-User-Access-Key when required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which plan tier is required for a project to use the Testim REST API?

options.text: Any plan tier — API access is universal.
API access requires no plan at all, it's a separate purchase.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's explicitly gated to one tier.
practiceQuiz.rationale: API access is a professional feature, available only to projects on the professional plan — not available by default on every tier.

optionExplanations.A: The API feature is plan gated.
optionExplanations.B: The professional plan is the documented requirement.
optionExplanations.C: It is not restricted to the free trial.
optionExplanations.D: The documentation ties API access to the professional plan.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When is the raw value of a newly generated API key visible?

options.text: It's always retrievable later from Settings → API.
Only once, at the moment it's generated — it must be copied immediately.
It's visible in every API response indefinitely.

practiceQuiz.rationale: The API key value is displayed only at generation time — you copy it then and click Done. It cannot be viewed again afterward; a new key would need to be generated if it's lost.

optionExplanations.A: The raw key is not displayed again after generation.
optionExplanations.B: Copy at generation and store securely; later management does not reveal the raw key.
optionExplanations.C: Weekly key emails are not documented.
optionExplanations.D: Responses do not disclose the key indefinitely.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How is the Testim REST API key used to authenticate a standard request?

options.text: As a query string parameter named apikey.
In Authorization: Bearer followed by the copied PAK-prefixed API key.
It isn't used for authentication at all.
As a cookie set manually by the developer.

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the copied complete key without adding a second prefix.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Authorization Bearer value is the copied API key. Encrypted-credential access has an additional authorized-user header, not replacement authentication.

optionExplanations.A: The documented authentication is a Bearer header, not an apikey query parameter.
optionExplanations.B: Send the copied full API key as the Bearer value.
optionExplanations.D: A manually created cookie is not the documented API-key mechanism.

quickRecap.value: REST API access is a professional-plan-only feature.
Settings → API → Generate API Key → copy immediately (shown once).
Authorization: Bearer followed by the complete copied API key (already PAK-prefixed).
Additionally supply authorized-user X-User-Access-Key; retain standard API authentication.
